A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title and contributor-focused terminology. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution scores, runtime measurements, counterfactual experiments, and generated-image comparisons on CIFAR-20, CelebA-HQ, and ArtBench, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, approximation diagnostics, alternative-unlearning experiments, and contributor analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions estimate Shapley values through constrained regression, pruning followed by recovery on the full dataset, and subset fine-tuning with the original diffusion loss. v2 expands the justification and evaluates alternatives without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The three dataset and task families remain. However, v1 Appendix A lists large omnivores and herbivores and medium mammals among CIFAR-20's superclasses; v2 Appendix B replaces these with flowers and household electrical devices. This revises reported category coverage without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated LOO, Banzhaf, LoRA fine-tuning, gradient-ascent, and influence-unlearning comparisons (Table 1 and Appendix F). Counterfactual comparator membership also changes: Figure 3 replaces CIFAR-20's D-TRAK with LOO, and CelebA-HQ's relative IF and gradient similarity with renormalized IF and pixel similarity.

E3.justification: v2 adds counterfactual experiments retaining only top contributors. Appendix D introduces Pearson-correlation evaluations using 100 subsets for model properties and 500 for Shapley estimates while varying fine-tuning steps. Appendix F.4 introduces FID comparisons against retrained models over 100 sampled subsets. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the original principal metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained subset-size and computational-budget analyses, v2 tests approximation quality versus fine-tuning steps, alternative valuation rules, and image preservation under different unlearning approaches. It also adds top-contributor case studies and distributions of image entropy, demographic embedding distance, and aesthetic quality (Appendices D and F.4–F.6).

E5.justification: Both versions report LDS means and 95% confidence intervals. v2 newly describes three independent held-out subset collections, although captions retain the three-random-initializations description. It also omits v1's explicit counterfactual repetition counts of ten initializations for CIFAR-20/CelebA-HQ and five for ArtBench. These reporting changes do not establish altered run counts.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the proposed method's LDS scores of 61.48%, 26.34%, and 61.44%, but revises several CelebA-HQ baselines; gradient similarity average changes from 25.93% to -18.32%. Table 4 changes CIFAR-20 FT at alpha=0.5 and 500 subsets from 20.57% to 39.60%. Numerous comparator, retention, correlation, FID, and contributor-analysis results are added. The revised CIFAR coverage description prevents treating its numerical differences as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds two asymptotic propositions and Appendix A's lemmas and proofs, absent from v1. Under convexity, smoothness, and bounded pruning-error assumptions, these claim bounds on model-property approximation and exact-Shapley error, including 2 sqrt(n) C. This is a substantial new theoretical component.

C1.justification: The central scientific contributions remain attribution of global diffusion-model properties to contributor groups, efficient Shapley estimation through pruning and fine-tuning, and superior attribution across three use cases. The revised compensation and labeling emphasis changes the motivation without materially changing these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting contributor importance to image entropy, minority demographic clusters, and aesthetic characteristics, and interprets alternative unlearning methods as degrading image quality. It explicitly limits the new theory to asymptotic, exact-Shapley settings and discusses extensions beyond diffusion models. The ethics statement adds substantive qualifications concerning privacy, consent, and biases that global metrics may not capture.

D1.justification: v2 specifies aggregation from local scores to contributor scores and adds an eight-RTX-6000 runtime accounting. It revises reported GPU memory capacities from 40/40/24 GB to 24/48/80 GB. Most optimizer, scheduler, package-version, and training-budget details are retained or relocated to Appendix C rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning Beta Shapley, the lottery ticket hypothesis, Attribute-to-delete, Inception Score interpretation, and artists and data labor, while removing some earlier background citations. These extend the motivation and theoretical positioning; the principal distinction from existing local, individual-datum diffusion attribution remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and method exposition around crediting contributors, replacing much group-attribution terminology. It separates baseline descriptions into their own main-text subsection, moves training details into an appendix, reorganizes the appendices, and replaces the brief concluding broader-impact appendix with a main-text ethics statement.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework schematic, expands Figure 3 with contributor-retention curves, and replaces the main generated-image displays with contributor examples and a composite comparison. It adds approximation plots, unlearning displays, distribution plots, and comparison tables. Several original appendix image grids remain under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical assessment through direct LOO/Banzhaf comparisons, approximation diagnostics, and contributor analyses. However, its new Proposition 1 proof incorrectly infers equality of model parameters from equal convex objective values after Equation (32); Proposition 2 inherits that step. The stronger empirical coverage and clearer exposition therefore coexist with an unsupported theoretical justification, making the net change in scientific quality uncertain.
